criterion: Coordinator round 2, items 2 (the sky part of the colonnade) and 3 (the relighting gallery without downloads, 2026-10-21): an analytic sky model, our own baked HDR environments (clear noon, overcast, golden hour, night with a moon) and one interior probe path-traced from our own scene, each recorded in a lockfile with its recipe and hash; and a relighting page that shows owned assets under each environment with their G-buffer channels.
written: 2026-10-21, before any code and before any run

design.sky: raw/renderer/sky.hpp, src/renderer/sky.cpp. Clear and hazy skies: the Preetham, Shirley and Smits model (SIGGRAPH 1999): the Perez luminance distribution with coefficients linear in turbidity, zenith luminance and chromaticity, xyY to linear Rec.709, in nits, transcribed from the paper's appendix (from memory; the checks below are what tie it down). Overcast: the CIE overcast sky, L = Lz (1 + 2 cos theta) / 3. The sun as a disk of 0.2667 degrees with an illuminance from a stated simple extinction; at night a moon disk of 0.26 degrees, a dim sky and stars placed by the noise module's white noise. All of it is ours; no measured HDRI.
design.bake: lighting::Cube level 0 from any sky function (texel centres), the same layout the image-lighting path reads. Environments: clear noon (turbidity 2.5, sun 70 degrees up), overcast (zenith 8,000 nits), golden hour (turbidity 4, sun 4 degrees up), night (moon 35 degrees up, stars). Interior probe: path tracer v2 cube faces rendered from inside retro_room at a fixed point.
design.lockfile: evidence/envmaps.lock.json: per map, the generator command, its parameters, the size and the SHA-256 of the cube's level-0 float64 data, with the compiler family that produced the hash
design.relight: raw_native_cli relight --out DIR: the sphere field and the material gallery under every environment (the float64 shading of the gallery path), with albedo, normal, roughness and depth channels, as PNGs and an index.html page

k1_clear_vs_cie.what: Preetham's relative luminance (divided by its zenith value) at turbidity 2.5 against the CIE standard clear sky (ISO 15469 type 12: Perez a -1, b -0.32, c 10, d -3, e 0.45), an independent standardised form, at 400 directions of the upper hemisphere more than 5 degrees from the sun, sun at 30 and 60 degrees elevation
k1_clear_vs_cie.bound: median relative difference at most 25%, worst at most 80%
k1_clear_vs_cie.prediction: holds; both are Perez fits to clear skies, with different coefficients

k2_overcast.what: the overcast sky's horizon over zenith luminance

k3_turbidity.what: luminance 10 degrees from the sun over zenith luminance, turbidity 2 against 6, sun 45 degrees up
k3_turbidity.bound: larger at 6 (haze brightens the circumsolar region)

k4_colour.what: clear noon zenith in linear Rec.709
k4_colour.bound: blue above red; overcast neutral within 1%

k5_bake.what: horizontal illuminance from each baked cube (texel solid angles) against direct integration of the sky function by 2^20 stratified directions, sun and moon disks excluded from both

k6_lockfile.what: regenerating every map from its recipe reproduces the SHA-256 recorded for the compiler family
k6_lockfile.prediction: holds for the analytic skies on the recording compiler; the probe depends on the C runtime's sin and cos and is recorded per family

k7_relight.bound: each environment visibly changes the lighting of every asset; reviewed by eye and recorded

does_not_prove: That the sky matches a measured sky (no measured data is used; if validation against a measured HDRI ever becomes necessary, that is a question for the author before any download); physical accuracy of the moon and stars (artistic, stated as such).
